Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From f125846ee79fcae537a964ce66494e96fa54a6de Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Luxiao Xu <rakukuip@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 13:12:42 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] rxrpc: fix reference count leak in rxrpc_server_keyring()

This patch fixes a reference count leak in rxrpc_server_keyring()
by checking if rx->securities is already set.

Fixes: 17926a79320a ("[AF_RXRPC]: Provide secure RxRPC sockets for use by userspace and kernel both")
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Co-developed-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Suggested-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Tested-by: Ren Wei <enjou1224z@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Luxiao Xu <rakukuip@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ren Wei <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
cc: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
cc: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
cc: linux-afs@lists.infradead.org
cc: stable@kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260408121252.2249051-15-dhowells@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/rxrpc/server_key.c b/net/rxrpc/server_key.c
index 36b05fd842a7..27491f1e1273 100644
--- a/net/rxrpc/server_key.c
+++ b/net/rxrpc/server_key.c
@@ -125,6 +125,9 @@ int rxrpc_server_keyring(struct rxrpc_sock *rx, sockptr_t optval, int optlen)
 
 	_enter("");
 
+	if (rx->securities)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (optlen <= 0 || optlen > PAGE_SIZE - 1)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
-- 
2.34.1

**Modifications in each file:**

- **`net/rxrpc/server_key.c`**: In the function `rxrpc_server_keyring()`, an early return check is added. If `rx->securities` is already non-NULL (i.e., a server keyring has already been set), the function now immediately returns `-EINVAL` without proceeding to parse or assign a new keyring.

**Relationships between modifications:**

- The addition prevents the function from being called multiple times successfully. Previously, calling `rxrpc_server_keyring()` more than once would overwrite the existing `rx->securities` pointer without releasing the previously held reference, causing a reference count leak on the key. By returning an error when `rx->securities` is already set, the fix ensures that the function can only be called once, thereby eliminating the leak.

2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug. 



Provide a response strictly in the following format:
Root cause:<Root cause>

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
rx->securities = key;
</text>
Reason:
The function rxrpc_server_keyring() can be called multiple times, and each time it assigns a new keyring pointer to rx->securities without first releasing the reference to the previous keyring. This causes a reference count leak because the old keyring is never dereferenced.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
if (rx->securities)
	return -EINVAL;
</text>
Reason:
This early check ensures that if a keyring has already been set (rx->securities is non‑NULL), the function immediately returns an error instead of proceeding to allocate and assign a new keyring. This prevents the overwrite and consequent reference leak.
